samples: This program is a fixed demo that downloads three example sites (example.com, .org and .net) in parallel, then prints each page's character count with the largest first. It then fetches two pages from example.com (the home page and /docs) under a 10-second limit and prints their combined size. The sites are hard-coded, it needs console and network access, and it aborts with an error if any request fails or the deadline passes, so it is more a template for concurrent fetching than a configurable tool.

This program downloads three fixed example sites (example.com, .org and .net) in parallel, then prints each page's character count with the largest first. It then fetches the example.com home page and its docs page together under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined size, so the home page is downloaded twice in total. It needs console and network access, fails if any download fails or the deadline passes, and takes no input, so it is a demo rather than a reusable tool. One thing to check before relying on it is that the combined-size line uses values created inside the concurrent block, which the language reference does not clearly show being usable after that block ends.

This program downloads three example web pages (example.com, .org and .net) in parallel and prints each address with the number of characters in its body, largest first. It then fetches the example.com home page and its docs page concurrently under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined character count, so example.com is downloaded twice. It needs console and network access, and it stops with an HTTP error or a timeout if any download fails or the deadline expires.

This program downloads three example websites in parallel, then prints each one's body length in characters, largest first. It then fetches the example.com home page and its docs page together under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined length, failing if any download fails or the deadline expires. One caveat: the final combined-size line uses two values created inside the concurrent block, and the cheat sheet doesn't say they stay visible after the block ends, so that part may not compile as written.

This program fetches three example websites in parallel, measures how many characters each page's body contains, and prints the sizes from largest to smallest. It then fetches two more pages (the example.com home page and its docs page) under a 10-second deadline and prints their combined size, and it only needs permission to use the network and the console. One caution: the final combined-size line uses results created inside the concurrent block, and the cheat sheet doesn't say those names remain visible after the block ends, so the checker may reject it. Check that before relying on the program.
